title: Shortwave Deploy Ops: Coda & Signature Checklist (6-hour window) — Draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact ops playbook for 6-hour "shortwave" deploys: quick, focused changes that must go live in a tight window with an on-call + handoff pattern. Goal: get a small release across the line with predictable safety nets, minimal blast radius, and clear sign-off points.

Scope:
- Applies to urgent hotfixes, small feature toggles, and timed configuration flips that can be completed in <= 6 hours.
- Not for schema migrations, heavy model swaps, or capacity-altering infra changes. Those follow the full release runbook.

High-level timeline (example window):
- T-2h: Finalize artifacts and run local smoke (dev/stage). Notify watchlist (Slack #deploys).
- T-90m: Preflight on canary subset (1% traffic) + telemetry warmup.
- T-60m: Operator & SRE alignment meeting (15m). Confirm rollback plan and throttles.
- T-30m: Safety lane checks & signatures from owner + SRE lead.
- T: Go-live -> ramp to 5% -> observe 15m -> ramp to 25% -> observe 30m -> full ramp if clear.
- T+3h: Post-ramp stabilization period and initial debrief.
- T+6h: Closeout, release notes published, follow-up issues triaged.

Preflight checklist (must be green before T-60m):
- [ ] Artifact builds completed and immutables tagged (image digest present).
- [ ] CI smoke + regression suite passing for changed components. Link: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/actions/runs/###
- [ ] Canary config prepared: traffic split, throttles, and feature-flag IDs.
- [ ] Healthcheck endpoints verified for new artifact (startup and /ready).
- [ ] Backfill/queued task impact assessed (no backlog spikes expected).
- [ ] Infra capacity: GPU/CPU headroom confirmed by SRE (>= 20% buffer).
- [ ] Observability: dashboards pinned, alert thresholds reviewed, synthetic checks ready.
- [ ] Rollback image and route are staged and tested.

Signature checklist (explicit human sign-off — signatures can be a Slack emoji + timestamp):
- Release owner (feature/PR author): confirms business readiness and acceptance tests.
- SRE lead: confirms capacity and rollback paths.
- Security/Compliance (if PII/tokens changed): quick ack or link to ticket.
- Product manager (if customer-visible change): approve messaging and release notes.
- Ops lead: confirms staffing and escalation points.

Operational watchlist during window (operator playbook):
- Primary operator watches latency histogram (p95/p99), error rate (4xx/5xx), and queue depth.
- Secondary operator focuses on resource signals: GPU utilization, memory pressure, pod restarts.
- Use synthetic golden request (idempotent, representative) every 30s — results logged to watch channel.
- Timed sentinels: 5m, 15m, 30m, 60m checks with snapshot upload to the runbook (attach telemetry links).
- Escalation path: operator -> SRE lead -> release owner -> on-call infra. Include pager numbers in Slack channel header.

Telemetry warmup and heartbeat sampling (distinctive shortwave pattern):
- Purpose: avoid false-positive spikes when switching traffic; ensure KV caches and prefix caches are populated predictably.
- Warmup steps:
  - T-90m: run 100 golden requests against canary nodes at ramped intervals (10s apart) to populate caches.
  - T-50m: sample model kv-cache hit rates and baseline token-latency (store baseline snapshot).
  - Streaming gauges: enable p95 token latency sampling at 5s granularity for the first 30m of ramp.
- Logging: tag warmup traces with "shortwave-warmup" to filter out noise from post-deploy graphs.

Ramp & rollback decision matrix (simplified):
- If error rate spike > 3x baseline OR p99 latency > baseline + 400ms sustained for 5m -> pause ramp and investigate.
- If spike persists > 15m after mitigations -> rollback to last stable artifact.
- If canary shows minor increase (<= 1.5x error) but root cause isolated and mitigated -> hold at current traffic for 30m before continuing.

Rollback quick commands (examples to capture in operator clipboard):
- kubectl set image deployment/model-service model=model:stable-digest --record
- routing toggle: curl -X POST https://router.internal/api/traffic -d '{"route":"stable"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
- ff toggle: redis-cli HSET feature-flags my-shortwave-feature false
(Operators should have pre-authorized keys; rotate after rocket launches.)

Draft release notes (shortwave format — concise for customer-facing channels):
- Title: Small fix: reduce tokenization edge-case retries (2026-10-12)
- Description: Fixes an intermittent retry loop seen on specific token boundaries that caused brief latency spikes for a subset of requests. This release reduces unnecessary retries and improves p95 latency for affected flows.
- Impact: Transparent to most users; expected reduction in p95 latency by ~20% for edge case requests. No data migration required.
- Rollout plan: Canary -> staged ramp -> full. Monitoring active.

Post-deploy closeout & follow-ups (T+3h to T+72h):
- [ ] Consolidate watch snapshots and upload as runbook attachment.
- [ ] Publish short release note (channels: #releases, intercom update if customer-facing).
- [ ] Create follow-up tickets for any issues observed during ramp (tag severity).
- [ ] Schedule retro if any threshold was breached or rollback occurred.

Postmortem triggers (auto-open):
- Any rollback that takes > 30m to effect or requires cross-team escalations.
- Customer-visible outage > 5 minutes in any region.
- Unexpected increase in cost (e.g., GPU utilization doubling for > 1 hour) linked to the change.

Open questions / TODOs (capture before finalizing):
- Who will own the synthetic golden request signatures in the long term? (assign by next sprint)
- Add shortwave checklist to the on-call rotation handbook (SRE doc).
- Validate that the telemetry warmup tags propagate to long-term dashboards (product ask).

Notes & references:
- Quick links: JIRA RELEASE-321, PR #542 (build artifacts), Confluence shortwave playbook draft.
- Small experimental pattern: "signature check" is intentionally lightweight here — a Slack reaction + timestamp suffices for audit; we can formalize later if compliance requires.

If you are on the watchlist for a shortwave: read this doc, confirm your signature, and be prepared for a 6-hour focused window. Keep communication crisp: post every sentinel snapshot to #deploys and tag the SRE lead.

-- Maya (release owner)
